title: Prescription Processing Allowance, Formulary Benefit Home-Delivery Transition Supplies
content:
Under the Formulary Benefit, a home-delivery transition supply carries an allowance for the time the home delivery pharmacy needs before it ships. The allowance turns on the prescriptions for the drug on file at the member's Home Delivery Pharmacy and on the latest shipped order of the drug.

## Clause

- **(a) New strength.** The home delivery pharmacy received a prescription for the drug after the latest shipped order (its received date is later than that order's date), at a strength different from that order's. The program's new-prescription processing time, in business days, is added as that number of days.
- **(b) Prescription on file.** No such new-strength prescription exists, but the drug has a prescription on file at the home delivery pharmacy. The program's refill processing time, in business days, is added as that number of days.
- **(c) Otherwise.** No processing allowance is added.

The prescription examined is the member's latest prescription for the drug at the home delivery pharmacy, by received date. The allowance is added to the supply before the supply is held between zero and the formulary's maximum days supply for one transition fill.

## Condition table

| Latest prescription received after the latest shipped order | Its strength differs from that order's | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | new-prescription processing time |
| yes | no | refill processing time |
| no (received on or before the order date) | any | refill processing time |
| no prescription on file | | none |

*Hypothetical.* Suppose the latest shipped order was 5 mg, and a 7.5 mg prescription was received afterwards. With a program new-prescription processing time of 3 business days, 3 days are added.
